title: Russia will launch a routine ISS supply mission tomorrow—apparently, it's a big secret
gist: NASA declined to confirm the date of Russia's Progress MS-36 ISS cargo launch, referring questions to Roscosmos, a break from its practice of televising Progress launches as recently as September. Eric Berger argues the secrecy likely originates with Roscosmos and stems from Russian fears of Ukrainian drone attacks on spaceports, and that it would be untenable for the crewed Soyuz MS-30 flight in March 2027.

insights.claim: The likely cause of Russia's new launch secrecy is the war against Ukraine, after drone attacks on the Plesetsk spaceport led the Russian government to tighten information about launches, a policy apparently extended to other spaceports.
